 Bailey Pemberton Sun, October 25, 2026 at 2:05 PM CDT 4 min read 8795.T -0.21% 
 8795 
 T&D Holdings has seen its share price move sharply over recent years, which puts a spotlight on whether the current valuation can be explained by the returns the insurer earns on its capital. For anyone looking at the stock today, the key question is how that share price lines up with the income the business is able to generate from every yen it reinvests. 
 Over the past 5 years the stock has returned about 286.7%, which makes it important to ask whether that kind of run is grounded in the underlying returns T&D Holdings earns on its capital base. 
 The group's long term value story hinges on how efficiently it can turn the premiums it collects and the assets it manages into profit, which can shape both reinvestment capacity and the durability of its capital returns. 
 Prefer to judge T&D Holdings on earnings? See why T&D Holdings's 16.0x P/E tells a different valuation story . 
 The issue now is whether the current share price fairly reflects the returns T&D Holdings generates on the capital it employs in the business. 
 To assess whether the returns T&D Holdings earns on its capital justify the current price, it can be useful to compare that same question across 14 high quality undervalued stocks 
 Is T&D Holdings Still Cheap on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model looks at how efficiently T&D Holdings turns its equity base into profits above the return that shareholders require. Here, the business is assumed to generate stable earnings of ¥360.71 per share on a Stable Book Value of ¥3,655.33 per share, which lines up with an Average Return on Equity of 9.87% based on analyst estimates. 
 What stands out for T&D Holdings is the gap between that profitability and the estimated Cost of Equity of ¥182.62 per share. The model attributes an Excess Return of ¥178.09 per share, indicating that the insurer is projected to earn more on its capital than the return investors are assumed to demand. With the current share price at ¥4,800.00 and the Excess Returns projections putting T&D Holdings' estimated intrinsic value substantially above the current share price, the market price implies a discount to these modeled capital returns.
